learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the heavy burden of patriarchal oppression on women and how art can be used as a powerful medium to express the desire for freedom.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Aunt Jennifer is embroidering a panel with bright yellow (topaz) tigers. These tigers are fearless, strong, proud, and 'chivalric'. They do not fear the men beneath the tree. They represent everything Aunt Jennifer wants to be.

main_concepts.concept_title: 💍 The Weight of the Wedding Band
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Aunt Jennifer's fingers are fluttering (trembling with fear and weakness) so much that she can barely pull the ivory needle. The 'massive weight of Uncle's wedding band' sits heavily upon her hand.
The wedding band is a metaphor for the oppressive, dominating nature of her husband and the patriarchal society. It has stripped her of her freedom, identity, and confidence.
The poet says that even when Aunt Jennifer dies, her terrified hands will still be 'ringed with ordeals'—she will carry the marks of her miserable, enslaved married life even into her grave.
While the creator (Aunt Jennifer) will die defeated and oppressed, her creations (the embroidered tigers) will continue to 'prance, proud and unafraid' forever, outliving her trauma.

fun_activity.title: 🎨 Symbolism Search
fun_activity.instructions: Aunt Jennifer sewed tigers to represent the freedom and strength she lacked. If you were creating an artwork to represent a trait you wish you had more of, what animal would you draw? Why?

exam_tips: 📌 Contrast is the biggest theme: The weak, trembling, fearful Aunt vs. the strong, confident, fearless tigers she creates.
📌 The 'Uncle's wedding band' doesn't just mean a physical ring; it symbolizes the crushing legal and social expectations placed on women in a male-dominated society.
📌 Poetic devices: Metaphor ('massive weight of Uncle's wedding band'), Synecdoche ('terrified hands' represents her whole terrified being).
quick_recap: ⭐ The poem highlights the loss of a woman's identity post-marriage in a traditional patriarchal setup.
⭐ The tigers are 'denizens of a world of green', meaning they are wild, free inhabitants of the forest, unlike Aunt who is trapped indoors.
⭐ Art serves as Aunt Jennifer's only escape mechanism from her grim reality.
